purpose: List possible RRArchive/PANDA reader surfaces for a future independent reader amendment. This inventory does not select, install, execute, pin, or authorize any reader and does not inspect an archive.

public_metadata_services_used: GitHub tag and commit metadata API

candidates.name: PANDA rrunpack.py
candidates.candidate_version: upstream tag v1.8.85 observed, not pinned
candidates.possible_use: Format-identification and RRArchive unpack compatibility candidate.
known_limitations: Its public identity is an unpack utility, not a bounded no-extract central-directory reader.
Direct use would conflict with the current no-extract and no-payload-persistence policy unless a later amendment proves a metadata-only dry-run or supplies a separately reviewed bounded adapter.
No executable, interpreter, dependency set, invocation, parser, output cap, or local SHA-256 is pinned.
Compatibility with the PANDAcap 2020 RRArchive variant is unverified.

candidates.name: PANDA native panda-system-* replay runtime
candidates.candidate_version: upstream tag v1.8.85 observed, not pinned
candidates.possible_use: Reference implementation for format compatibility if a future authorization permits a sandboxed synthetic compatibility test.
known_limitations: Replay is active execution, not a passive archive metadata read.
It may require an architecture-matched PANDA build, guest state, kernel profile, and format-compatible recording.
Running a honeypot replay could expose commands, credentials, payload behavior, secrets, personal identifiers, or malicious activity.
It is unsuitable for the planned first-pass central-directory and notice audit unless a future authority explicitly permits replay inside a separately isolated environment.
No executable build identity, dependency graph, invocation, parser, output cap, or local SHA-256 is pinned.

candidates.name: PANDA rr_print
candidates.candidate_version: upstream tag v1.8.85 observed, not pinned
candidates.possible_use: Low-level RR log parser candidate only after outer-container and privacy Gates are separately closed.
known_limitations: The public tree identifies source code, not a prebuilt, reproducibly pinned executable.
It is an RR log printer rather than a verified outer RRArchive central-directory reader.
Printed event or nondeterminism data may reveal ordinary replay content and therefore exceed a notice or manifest-only audit.
It may require archive unpacking or native PANDA build artifacts, both outside current authority.
No build flags, executable identity, invocation, parser, redaction policy, output cap, or local SHA-256 is pinned.

candidates.name: pandare Python interface
candidates.possible_use: Potential controller for a future pinned PANDA runtime; direct RRArchive metadata-read capability is unverified.
known_limitations: The PyPI metadata describes a Python interface to PANDA, not a standalone passive RRArchive reader.
Using it would likely require native PANDA components and could initiate active replay.
The package index version alone does not pin every wheel, sdist, dependency, executable, or transitive native artifact.
No method-level reader contract, invocation, parser, privacy boundary, output cap, or artifact SHA-256 is pinned.
This candidate must be rejected if a future source inspection cannot prove a bounded metadata-only path.

preferred_future_review_order: Determine whether rrunpack.py can expose format identity without extraction; otherwise reject it for the first-pass audit.
Seek a passive, bounded, no-extract RRArchive metadata parser before considering active PANDA replay.
Treat rr_print and pandare as later compatibility or content-parser candidates, not notice or manifest readers.
future_reader_amendment_must_pin: reader name and exact version or commit
source and local executable or package identity
member, token, per-member, total-byte, time, and output limits
privacy, secret, identifier, malware, and raw-path redaction
fail-closed behavior on unsupported format or cap exceedance
